Rip current warning: no swimming at the north end, by the red flags.
A rip current is a strong, narrow stream of water that flows away from the shore.
If a current pulls you, swim sideways, along the beach, not against it. Then wave to a lifeguard.
Swim only between the green flags. Lifeguards are there from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
Dogs must be on a leash. Dogs are not allowed in the tide pools.

passages.title: Story Woods Trail Notice
sentences: From April 1 to June 15, the Creek Trail in Story Woods is closed between the old mill and the campsite.
A pair of great blue herons has built a large nest of sticks high in a pine tree beside the trail.
Herons are easily disturbed while they are nesting, and if people walk too close, the parents may leave and the eggs can get cold.
Park rangers have put up a rope fence and orange signs at both ends of the closed section.
Hikers can still reach the campsite by using the Ridge Trail, which is the only other route.
The Ridge Trail is 1.5 miles longer than the Creek Trail, and it climbs a steep, rocky hill.
Allow about 45 extra minutes of walking, and carry additional water on warm afternoons.
Cyclists may use the Ridge Trail, but they must walk their bikes up the steepest section.
During the nesting season, dogs must remain on a leash on every trail in Story Woods.
Visitors who would like to observe the herons can use the viewing deck behind the old mill.
The deck is about 300 feet from the nest, a distance that keeps the birds calm.
Free binoculars hang on hooks at the deck, and a ranger answers questions there on Saturday mornings.
Please speak quietly on the deck, and never use a camera flash, because a sudden light can startle the birds.
The trail may reopen early if the young herons leave the nest before June 15.
Rangers will post any change on the information board in the Story Woods parking lot.
Thank you for helping the herons raise their chicks in peace.

rows: Bring a flashlight with a red light only. Red light does not spoil your night vision.
Your eyes need about 20 minutes in the dark to see faint stars. White light starts that time over.
Never point a telescope or binoculars at the Sun, even near sunset.

passages.title: Eclipse Day
sentences: Next Monday afternoon, the Moon will pass in front of part of the Sun.
This is called a partial solar eclipse, and Harbor Town will see it from 1:10 PM to 3:40 PM.
At 2:25 PM, the Moon will cover the biggest part of the Sun.
Lantern Peaks Observatory will give out free eclipse glasses at the library on Saturday.
Never look straight at the Sun without eclipse glasses, not even for a few seconds.
During a partial eclipse, part of the Sun is always uncovered, and its light can hurt your eyes.
Regular sunglasses are not safe, even very dark ones.
Before you use eclipse glasses, check them for scratches or holes.
If they are damaged, do not use them.
Put the glasses on before you look up, and look away from the Sun before you take them off.
Do not look through a telescope, binoculars or a camera while you wear eclipse glasses.
These tools gather the Sun's light and make it much stronger, so it can burn through the glasses.
If you do not have glasses, you can make a pinhole viewer.
Poke a small hole in a card, stand with your back to the Sun, and let the light shine through the hole onto a sheet of paper.
You will see a small, bright circle on the paper, with a dark piece missing where the Moon covers the Sun.

rows: Air: Squeeze each tire. It should feel firm. Soft tires make the bike hard to steer.
Brakes: Squeeze each brake lever. The lever should stop before it touches the handlebar.
Chain: Turn the pedals backward. The chain should run smoothly, with no rust and no loud clicks.
Helmet: It should sit level, about two fingers above your eyebrows.
The side straps should make a V under each ear. Buckle the chin strap so only one finger fits under it.
If the brakes fail the check, do not ride. Walk the bike home or to the shop.
If a tire is a little soft, pump it to the number printed on the side of the tire.

visual.title: Band Room: Protect Your Hearing
rows: Drums and brass instruments can be as loud as a lawn mower, or louder.
Loud sound for a long time can hurt your hearing, and that damage does not heal.
Wear earplugs when you play drums for more than 15 minutes, and during every full band practice.
Foam earplugs are in the green box by the door. Take a new pair each day.
How to put in a foam earplug: Roll it into a thin, tight tube with clean fingers.
Reach over your head and gently pull the top of your ear up and back.
Slide the earplug in, then hold it for 20 seconds while it grows to fill your ear.
If your ears ring after practice, tell Ms. Gray.

passages.title: Robot Rally Rules
sentences: Welcome to the Harbor Town Robot Rally!
Everyone who enters the pit area must put on safety glasses, including visitors.
You may take them off only in the lunch room or outside.
Carry robots on a cart or in two hands, and never drive a robot in the hallways.
Every robot must pass a safety check before its first match.
At the check table, a judge will look for loose wires and sharp edges.
The judge will also test the red stop button, which must cut all power to the robot at once.
A robot that fails the check may be fixed and checked again, as many times as the team needs.
Charge battery packs only at the charging station by the stage, where a volunteer watches them.
During a match, only the drivers may stand inside the white box.
If a robot moves in a way you did not expect, press its stop button.
Do not reach into the arena or try to grab a moving robot.
Wait until the referee says the arena is safe, and then you may pick up your robot.

visual.title: Gull Point Kayak Rentals
rows: Open 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM. All kayaks must be back on the sand by 6:00 PM.
Rentals last 1 hour or 2 hours. Pay at the hut before you go out.
Everyone must wear a life jacket, zipped and buckled, for the whole trip.
Paddlers under 16 must be in a group with an adult, in another kayak or in the same kayak.
Stay inside the yellow buoys. The water past them has strong currents and boats.
Wind flag: Green means rentals are open. Red means no rentals until the wind drops.
If your kayak tips over, stay with it. Hold on to it and wave your paddle in the air. A guard in the rescue boat will come to you.

Turn on Battery Saver to make your battery last longer. The map still works, but photos and videos turn off.
If you cannot find the trail, stay where you are and call for help. Staying in one place makes you easier to find.

passages.title: Knife Rules at Cooking Club
sentences: Welcome to the Harbor Middle School Cooking Club!
This week, each team will chop vegetables for an enormous pot of vegetable soup.
Sharp knives are important tools, and a sharp knife is actually safer than a dull one, because it slices cleanly instead of slipping.
Always cut on a cutting board, never on a plate or in your hand.
Place a damp paper towel underneath the board so that it cannot slide.
Hold the food with your fingertips bent under, so the side of the blade touches your knuckles and not your fingertips.
This careful position is called the claw grip.
If a knife starts to fall, step back and let it drop, and never try to catch it.
To carry a knife, hold the handle with the blade pointing down, next to your leg.
Say the words "Knife behind you" when you walk past someone.
Never put a knife into a sink full of soapy water, because another person could reach in without seeing it.
Wash it separately, dry it carefully, and return it to the knife block.

visual.title: Create a password
rows: Use at least 12 characters. Letters, numbers, spaces and symbols all count.
Do not use your name, your pet's name or your birthday. Other people can guess them.
A good idea: join 4 or more words that have nothing to do with each other.
Use a different password for every account.
Never share your password with friends. You may share it with a parent.

passages.title: Watch or Warning?
sentences: The Harbor Town Weather Service uses two different words when a big winter storm may be on its way.
A winter storm watch means that a storm is possible in the next two days, but forecasters are not yet certain where it will go.
A winter storm warning means that heavy snow or ice is already falling or is expected very soon, usually within a day.
A simple way to remember the difference is this: a watch means be prepared, and a warning means act now.
During a watch, families can check that they have flashlights, fresh batteries, warm blankets, and enough food and water for three days.
Phones and tablets should be fully charged, in case the power goes out.
Pet owners should also store extra food for their animals.
When a warning begins, the safest place to be is indoors.
Roads can become icy and slippery, so trips that are not necessary should wait until plows have cleared the streets.
If you must go outside, wear layers, a hat and gloves, because cold wind can damage bare skin quickly.
Never use a grill or a camp stove inside a house or a garage to stay warm, because they give off a harmful gas that you cannot see or smell.
Harbor Middle School will post any closing on its website by 6:00 AM.
The ferry does not run during a winter storm warning, and Captain Ruth Lane posts the next sailing time at the dock.
When the warning ends, wait for an adult to say that the sidewalks are safe before you go out to play in the snow.

passages.title: Old Mine Openings
sentences: More than a hundred years ago, miners dug for copper in the hills of Lantern Peaks.
When the copper ran out, the miners left, but many of their tunnels and shafts are still there.
A shaft is a hole that goes straight down into the ground, sometimes deeper than a ten-story building is tall.
Today, Ridgeway Mine Museum is the only old mine in the hills that is safe to enter, because workers check its walls, air and lights every day.
Old mine openings can look like small caves or shallow holes, but they are very different inside.
Wooden beams that once held up the roof may be rotten, and rocks can fall without warning.
The air deep inside may not have enough oxygen, and you cannot see or smell the difference.
Some shafts are hidden by bushes or covered with old boards that look solid but can break.
For these reasons, the rule for old mines is simple: stay out, and stay away from the edges.
Hikers on the Lantern Peaks trails may see orange signs that say DANGER: OLD MINE.
If you find an opening that has no sign, do not go near it, and do not throw rocks into it.
Instead, mark the spot on your map or write down the nearest trail sign, and tell a park ranger.
Rangers will put up a fence or a gate to keep people out.
Bats often live in old mines, and some sleep there all winter.
The gates over mine openings have bars spaced so that bats can fly through, but people cannot get in.
If you want to explore underground, take the tunnel tour at Ridgeway Mine Museum with Mr. Varga, who knows every safe path.

Today, ferries leave Harbor Town at 9:30 AM, 12:00 PM and 2:30 PM.
The trip to Gull Island takes 60 minutes in fog, not the usual 40 minutes.
The outer deck is closed. Please stay in the cabin and keep the doors shut.
You will hear the ship's horn every 2 minutes. This is normal in fog. It lets other boats know where we are.
Dogs must stay on a leash and inside the cabin.
If the fog gets thicker, Captain Ruth Lane may cancel a ferry. Changes will be posted on this board and in the Harbor Town Ferry app.
Tickets for a canceled ferry can be used on any ferry for 30 days.

passages.title: Fossil Dig Day
sentences: On Saturday, Dr. Bell and the museum team will lead a fossil dig for families at Shell Cliff Quarry.
The quarry's rocks formed on the floor of a shallow sea about 70 million years ago, when dinosaurs lived nearby.
Most fossils here are seashells, shark teeth and bits of plants, but last spring a visitor found part of a dinosaur's toe bone.
Every digger must wear a hard hat and safety glasses, which the museum will lend you at the gate.
Wear long pants and boots with closed toes, because the ground is covered with sharp stones.
Stay out of the area behind the orange fence, where the cliff face is loose and pieces of rock can fall.
Bring at least two bottles of water and wear sunscreen, since the quarry has no shade.
You may keep up to five shells or shark teeth that you find in the dig pile.
Any bone, and any fossil larger than your hand, belongs to the museum so that scientists can study it.
If you uncover something that might be a bone, do not dig it out yourself, because bones break easily when they are pulled from rock.
Instead, put a yellow flag next to it and call a museum worker, who will help you remove it carefully.
If your find is important, your name will go on its label when it is shown in the museum.
The dig runs from 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM, and children under 12 must stay with an adult the whole time.
If anyone sees lightning or hears thunder, everyone must walk back to the cars right away.

passages.title: Climbing Wall Rules
sentences: Leo and Ana visit the climbing wall at the Harbor Town Rec Center.
A staff member points to the board before they climb.

visual.title: Climbing Wall: Read Before You Climb
rows: Climbers must be 8 or older. Climbers under 14 need an adult to sign a safety form first.
Wear a harness. A staff member checks every harness before your first climb.
Clip the auto-belay to the front loop of your harness. Check that the gate on the clip is fully closed.
An auto-belay is a rope machine. It holds you if you slip, and it lowers you slowly when you let go.
Only one climber on each rope at a time. Never climb above or below another person.
Shoes: climbing shoes or clean sneakers. No bare feet and no sandals.
Empty your pockets before you climb. Phones and keys can fall on people below.
Green routes are easy, blue routes are medium, and black routes are hard. Start on green.
When you reach the top, let go of the wall and lean back. The auto-belay will lower you.

passages.title: Campsite Food Lockers
sentences: Story Woods is home to raccoons, foxes, skunks and mice, and all of them have an excellent sense of smell.
A raccoon can smell food inside a closed cooler, and its clever paws can open zippers, lids and even some latches.
When wild animals eat food from people, they can get sick, and they may stop being careful around people.
Animals that get people food often come back to campsites again and again, looking for more.
Every campsite in Story Woods has a metal food locker with a heavy latch.
Store all food, drinks, trash and cooking pots in the locker whenever you are not eating.
Also store anything with a strong smell, such as toothpaste, sunscreen, soap and bug spray, because animals may think it is food.
Never keep food or scented things in your tent, not even a granola bar in a backpack pocket.
Close the latch every time, even if you will be gone for only a few minutes.
Never feed wild animals, even if they come very close and seem friendly.
If a raccoon or a fox walks into your campsite, stand up, speak in a loud voice, and give it space to leave.
Do not chase it or try to touch it, and keep pets on a leash so that they stay calm and safe.
If an animal seems sick, acts strangely, or will not leave, move away from it and tell a ranger at the campsite office.

passages.title: Concert Video Rules
sentences: Leo plays drums with the Grade 7 band at the spring concert tonight.

visual.title: Spring Concert: Photos and Videos
rows: You may film your own child. Please do not film other students up close.
Some students have a blue star sticker on their music folder. Their families asked that they not appear in any photos or videos.
No flash, and no bright screens held up high, during the music. Lights bother the players and the people behind you.
You may take flash photos during the bows at the end of each song.
Post concert videos only on the Harbor Middle family page, which only school families can see.
Do not post videos on public sites, where anyone can watch them.
Ms. Gray will share a full recording of the concert with every family next week.

passages.title: Kitchen Helper Rules
sentences: On Saturdays, Sam and Maya help Grandma Rose at the bakery.

visual.title: Rose's Bakery: Kitchen Helper Rules
rows: Wash your hands with soap for 20 seconds before you start, and again after you touch eggs, raw dough or trash.
Tie back long hair and wear an apron.
Use only dry oven mitts. A wet mitt lets heat through quickly and can burn your hand.
Turn the mixer off and wait for the beater to stop moving before you scrape the bowl or touch the beater.
Do not taste raw dough or batter. Raw eggs and raw flour can make people sick.
The back table is for nut-free baking. Wash your hands before you work there, and never bring nuts, nut butters or tools from other tables to it.
If you spill something, put out the yellow Wet Floor sign before you get the mop.
Ask Grandma Rose before you use the oven, the big mixer or any knife.

The library building across the street

items.prompt: Suppose Leo starts the free trial and forgets to cancel. What happens after 7 days?

The card is charged $9, and then $9 again every month

items.prompt: Maya is 11, and she is wearing sandals. What must she do to go on the tunnel tour?

Borrow rubber boots, wear a hard hat, and stay next to her dad
Borrow rubber boots and a hard hat, then walk the tour by herself
Skip the tour, because sandals are not allowed in the tunnel

items.explain: Maya must borrow rubber boots, wear a hard hat and stay next to her dad. Everyone wears a hard hat, visitors without closed shoes can borrow boots, and visitors under 12 stay next to their adult.

items.prompt: Maya sees a shiny gold-colored rock on the tunnel floor. She wants a rock to take home. What should she do?

Step past the yellow ropes to look for a bigger one
Ask the guide to pick it up for her
Leave it there, and take one rock from the Free Rock Bin at the gift shop

items.prompt: They reach Gull Point at 11:40 AM. What is the latest time they can stay at the tide pools?
items.hint: Find the time of low tide. Then read the rule about when the tide pools close, and add the time it gives.
items.explain: They can stay until 1:30 PM. Low tide is at 12:30 PM, and the tide pools are open until 1 hour after low tide. After that, the water covers the path back to the stairs.

items.prompt: Grandma Rose wants to swim after lunch. Which plan follows the board?

Swim between the green flags at 3:00 PM
Swim by the red flags at 3:00 PM
Swim at the north end at 11:00 AM

items.explain: She should swim between the green flags at 3:00 PM. The board says to swim only between the green flags, and lifeguards are there from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM. The red flags at the north end mark the rip current.

items.prompt: Sam, Pixel and Grandma Rose spend the day at Gull Point. Sort what they do.

cards.text: Pixel walks on a leash on the sand
Pixel splashes in a tide pool
Sam looks at a crab, then leaves it in its pool
Sam takes a sea star home in a bucket
They stay on the rocks until 2:00 PM
They walk back up the stairs at 1:15 PM

items.hint: Match each card to a rule about dogs, animals or tide pool times. For the times, work out when the tide pools close.
items.explain: Walking Pixel on a leash, leaving the crab and going back at 1:15 PM follow the board. Pixel in a tide pool, taking a sea star and staying until 2:00 PM break the rules, because dogs stay out of the pools, animals stay where you found them, and the pools close at 1:30 PM.

items.prompt: On May 10, Sam wants to walk with Pixel from the old mill to the campsite. Which plan follows the notice?
options: Take the Creek Trail with Pixel on a leash, because leashed dogs are allowed
Take the Ridge Trail with Pixel on a leash, and allow about 45 extra minutes
Take the Ridge Trail, and let Pixel off the leash on the steepest section
Wait until June 15, because every trail in Story Woods is closed

items.explain: Sam should take the Ridge Trail with Pixel on a leash and allow about 45 extra minutes. May 10 is inside the closing, the second paragraph names the Ridge Trail as the only other route and gives the extra time, and dogs must remain on a leash on every trail.

items.prompt: Maya wants to draw the herons. Which plan follows the notice?
options: Walk past the rope fence to get a closer view of the nest
Go to the viewing deck, take photos with a flash, and draw from the photos
Wait at the parking lot board until the trail opens
Go to the viewing deck behind the old mill, borrow binoculars, and draw quietly

items.explain: Maya should go to the viewing deck, borrow binoculars and draw quietly. The third paragraph says to visit the deck, that free binoculars hang there, and to speak quietly and never use a camera flash.

items.prompt: Leo asks why people must stay away from the nest. Tap the sentence that gives the reason.
items.hint: Read the first paragraph. Look for a sentence that says what could happen if people walk too close.
items.explain: Tap the sentence that says herons are easily disturbed while nesting, and if people walk too close, the parents may leave and the eggs can get cold. It is in the first paragraph.

items.prompt: What should Ana bring to her game?

A water bottle
A winter coat

Leave it open

Drive it again fast
Wait 5 minutes

A customer
Grandma Rose

To record Sam singing a song
To find out where Sam lives

TuneUp will tune the guitar by itself

1 GB
2 GB

Delete the videos fast

Walk around the end of the gate

Let the train go past.
Wait until the gates go all the way up.
Look both ways, then cross.

Nothing, because sunscreen lasts all day

At 11:15 AM

The real fossils in the glass case

Put it back on its picture

Ana cannot play Goal Rush anymore

Go to the snack bar and buy a drink
Wait for the horn to stop, then decide

Make a small fire in the circle of rocks

All walk to the creek, because 10 minutes is a short time

Hit the rock gently without glasses
Wear her sunglasses instead
Borrow a pair from the blue box

At least 10 steps away
Right next to the rock
2 steps away, with her glasses on

Charge it on her desk in the same room
Charge it on her bed next to her

Charge it with the yellow charger
Stop, do not charge it, and tell an adult

Leave it plugged in until 5:00 PM
Leave it plugged in all night
Plug in a second charger

items.explain: She should unplug it now. The fourth line says to unplug it when the light turns green. About 1 hour is only how long it usually takes.

items.prompt: Ben wants to keep the photo, but he does not want strangers to see it. Tap the button he should press.

Everyone who uses DinoWalk could see his face and his bedroom
The Triceratops in the photo is too small

items.prompt: Sam and his dad usually bike on Mill Road to the library. What should they do today?

Walk their bikes through the water
Bike on Mill Road, because the water looks shallow
Bike on Hill Street instead

The water is too cold for his bike tires
The library is closed until 8:00 PM
Bikes are never allowed on Mill Road

After 8:00 PM
Right after they tap Dismiss
As soon as the rain stops

items.prompt: Which light should Sam bring to the star party?
options: His phone's flashlight
A flashing bike light
A flashlight with a red light
A very bright white flashlight
items.hint: Find the rule about flashlights. What color of light does it name?
items.explain: Sam should bring a flashlight with a red light. The first rule says to bring a red light only, because red light does not spoil your night vision.

items.prompt: After 15 minutes in the dark, Priya turns on her phone's bright white screen. What happens?
options: She can see faint stars better
Her eyes need only 5 more minutes
Nothing changes, because she only looked for a moment
Her eyes must start the 20 minutes over

items.explain: Her eyes must start the 20 minutes over. The second rule says white light starts that time over.

items.prompt: Leo wants to look at the sunset with binoculars. What does the rule say?

Point them at the Sun only at sunset
Point them at the Sun for one second only
Point them at the Sun with sunglasses on

items.prompt: Sam finds his eclipse glasses from last year. One lens has a tiny scratch. What should he do?

Not use them, and get a new free pair at the library on Saturday
Use them, because the scratch is very small
Wear them over his sunglasses to make them safer

The binoculars will show the Moon, not the Sun
The binoculars make the Sun's light stronger, and it can burn through the glasses
The glasses make the view too dark to see anything

Stand with your back to the Sun.
Let the light shine through the hole onto a sheet of paper.
Look at the small, bright circle on the paper.
items.hint: Find the sentence that tells how to make a pinhole viewer. Its steps come in the same order as the words.
items.explain: First poke a small hole in a card, then stand with your back to the Sun. Next let the light shine through the hole onto paper, and last look at the bright circle on the paper. The steps are in the third paragraph.

items.prompt: Ben has 3 races left in the cup. Each race takes about 6 minutes. What is the best plan?
options: Tap Save and Quit in the menu now, and finish the cup tomorrow
Keep racing, because 15 minutes is enough for 3 races
Keep racing, and tap Ask for More Time after the game closes
Tap OK and race as fast as he can
items.hint: Work out how many minutes 3 races take. Compare it with the time left. Then check what happens if the game closes in the middle of a cup.
items.explain: Ben should tap Save and Quit now and finish the cup tomorrow. Three races take about 18 minutes, but he has only 15 minutes left. If the game closes in the middle of the cup, he starts the cup again from race 1.

items.prompt: Ben taps Ask for More Time right away. His mom answers 10 minutes later. How much game time does Ben have left when she answers?
options: None, because the game closed
About 5 minutes
15 minutes, because the time stopped
About 10 minutes
items.hint: Read the line about Ask for More Time. Does the time stop or keep running while he waits?
items.explain: About 5 minutes. The box says his time keeps running while he waits for an answer, and 15 minutes minus 10 minutes is 5 minutes.

items.prompt: No one gives Ben more time today. Tap the line that tells him when he can play again.
items.hint: Look for a line with a time of day in it.
items.explain: Tap the sixth line. It says game time starts again tomorrow at 7:00 AM.

items.prompt: Sam squeezes his back brake lever, and it touches the handlebar. His front tire is a little soft. What should he do?
options: Pump the tire, then ride to the shop slowly
Ride slowly and use only the front brake
Pump the tire, because a soft tire is the bigger problem
Walk the bike to the shop, because the brakes failed the check
items.hint: There are two problems. Find the line for each one. Which line says do not ride?
items.explain: Sam should walk the bike to the shop. The brake lever touched the handlebar, so the brakes failed the check, and the card says not to ride. Pumping the tire does not fix the brakes.

items.prompt: Sam puts on his helmet. Four fingers fit between his eyebrows and the front of the helmet. What does this tell him?
options: The helmet sits too far back, so he should move it forward and lower
The helmet sits just right
The chin strap is too tight
The helmet sits too low over his eyes
items.hint: Find the line about where the helmet should sit. Compare two fingers with four fingers.
items.explain: The helmet sits too far back, so he should move it forward and lower. The card says it should sit about two fingers above your eyebrows, and four fingers is too high.

items.prompt: Sort what Sam finds when he checks his bike and helmet.

cards.text: Both brake levers stop before the handlebar
Both tires feel firm
The chain is rusty and makes loud clicks
One finger fits under the chin strap
The side straps hang loose below his ears
The helmet sits four fingers above his eyebrows

items.hint: Match each card to its line on the card. Does it meet what the line says, or not?
items.explain: Brakes that stop before the handlebar, firm tires and one finger under the chin strap pass the check. A rusty, clicking chain, loose side straps and a helmet four fingers above the eyebrows must be fixed first.

items.prompt: The twins' first game is at 9:00 AM on Saturday. Their second game is at 1:00 PM on Saturday. When will they play?
options: Both games on Sunday
9:00 AM on Sunday and 1:00 PM on Saturday
9:00 AM on Saturday and 1:00 PM on Sunday
Both games on Saturday, as planned
items.hint: Check each game time against the advisory times. Then read what happens to games in each group.
items.explain: They play at 9:00 AM on Saturday and at 1:00 PM on Sunday. Games before 11:00 AM stay as planned, and games between 11:00 AM and 7:00 PM move to Sunday at the same time.

items.prompt: During the 9:00 AM game, Ana feels dizzy and very tired. What should she do?
options: Keep playing until the next water break
Drink a whole bottle of water fast, then keep playing
Lie down on the field until the feeling goes away
Stop playing, sit in the shade, sip water and tell Coach Novak
items.hint: Find the line that starts with If you feel dizzy. Read every step it gives.
items.explain: Ana should stop playing, sit in the shade, sip water and tell Coach Novak. The sixth line gives these steps.

items.prompt: Ben packs his bag on Friday night. Tap what every player needs to bring.
items.hint: Find the line that says what every player needs. Check how many, and how full.
items.explain: Ben must bring two full water bottles. The fourth line says every player needs two full water bottles.

items.prompt: Put Leo's steps for putting in an earplug in order.
steps: Take a new pair from the green box.
Roll the earplug into a thin, tight tube.
Pull the top of your ear up and back.
Slide the earplug in.
Hold it for 20 seconds.
items.hint: Start with where the earplugs are kept. Then follow the How to steps from top to bottom.
items.explain: Take a new pair from the green box, roll the earplug thin, pull the top of your ear up and back, slide it in, and hold it for 20 seconds. The steps are in the fourth to seventh lines.

items.prompt: Which student must wear earplugs, by the rules on the notice?
options: Ana, choosing trumpet music from the shelf for 20 minutes
Ben, carrying a keyboard into the band room
A trombone player in a 40-minute full band practice
Leo, playing drums alone for 10 minutes
items.hint: The rule about earplugs names two times. Check each student against both.
items.explain: The trombone player must wear earplugs. The third line says to wear them during every full band practice. Leo plays drums for only 10 minutes, and the drum rule starts at more than 15 minutes.

items.prompt: Leo forgot to wear earplugs today. After practice, his ears are ringing. What should he do?
options: Wait until the ringing stops and tell no one
Play louder next time so his ears get used to it
Use the earplugs from last week that are in his pocket
Tell Ms. Gray, and take a new pair of earplugs from the box next time
items.hint: Find the line about ringing ears. Then find the line about where to get earplugs and how often.
items.explain: Leo should tell Ms. Gray and take a new pair from the box next time. The last line says to tell Ms. Gray if your ears ring, and the fourth line says to take a new pair each day.

items.prompt: Priya's rover fails the safety check because a wire is loose. What can her team do?
options: Fix the wire and bring the rover back to the check table
Skip the check, because only one wire is loose
Drive the rover in its first match and fix it later
Leave the rally, because a robot gets only one check
items.hint: Find the sentence about a robot that fails the check.
items.explain: They can fix the wire and bring the rover back to the check table. The second paragraph says a robot that fails may be fixed and checked again, as many times as the team needs.

items.prompt: During a match, Priya's rover suddenly turns and drives toward the wall. Priya is a driver in the white box. What should she do?
options: Wait for the match to end, then press the stop button
Press the rover's stop button
Reach into the arena and grab the rover
Ask the referee if she may grab the rover
items.hint: Read the third paragraph. Find what to do when a robot moves in a way you did not expect.
items.explain: Priya should press the rover's stop button. The third paragraph says to press the stop button if a robot moves in a way you did not expect, and not to grab a moving robot.

items.prompt: Leo visits Priya in the pit area. He wants to know where he can take off his safety glasses. Tap the sentence that tells him.
items.hint: Read the first paragraph. Look for the words take them off.
items.explain: Tap the third sentence. It says you may take them off only in the lunch room or outside.

items.prompt: The twins want to paddle together in one kayak while their mom waits on the sand. What does the board say?
options: They may, because there are two of them
They may, if they both wear life jackets
They may, if they stay inside the yellow buoys
They may not, because paddlers under 16 need an adult with them on the water
items.hint: Find the rule with an age in it. The twins are 12. Where must the adult be?
items.explain: They may not. The fourth rule says paddlers under 16 must be in a group with an adult, in another kayak or in the same kayak. Their mom would be on the sand, not in a kayak.

items.prompt: The wind flag is green. The family wants to go out at 4:30 PM. Which rental can they choose?
options: Only the 1-hour rental
Only the 2-hour rental
Either rental
No rental, because the hut closes at 4:30 PM
items.hint: Add each rental time to 4:30 PM. Then check when the kayaks must be back.
items.explain: Only the 1-hour rental. One hour ends at 5:30 PM, but two hours would end at 6:30 PM, and all kayaks must be back by 6:00 PM.

items.prompt: Ben's kayak tips over inside the buoys. What should he do?
options: Take off his life jacket so he can climb back in
Stay with the kayak, hold on, and wave his paddle in the air
Let go of the kayak and swim to the beach
Swim past the buoys to reach a boat
items.hint: Find the rule that starts with If your kayak tips over.
items.explain: Ben should stay with the kayak, hold on and wave his paddle. The last rule says this, and a guard in the rescue boat will come to him.

items.prompt: Sam wants to take a long video of the waterfall. Which plan is best?
options: Turn on Battery Saver, then take the video
Tap Close and look for the trail without the map
Skip the video, turn on Battery Saver, then tap Guide Me Back
Take the long video first, then tap Guide Me Back
items.hint: Check the battery number. Then read what Battery Saver does and what Guide Me Back does.
items.explain: Sam should skip the video, turn on Battery Saver and tap Guide Me Back. The battery is at 15%. Battery Saver makes it last longer and turns videos off, but the map still works, and Guide Me Back shows arrows to the trail.

items.prompt: They reach the Ridge Trail at 6:00 PM and walk straight to the parking lot. About when will they get there?
options: About 7:10 PM, at sunset
About 6:20 PM
About 7:50 PM, after sunset
About 6:50 PM, before sunset
items.hint: Find how long 2 miles takes. Add it to 6:00 PM. Then compare with the sunset time.
items.explain: About 6:50 PM, before sunset. The box says most hikers walk 2 miles in about 50 minutes, and 6:00 PM plus 50 minutes is 6:50 PM. Sunset is at 7:10 PM.

items.prompt: Suppose Sam and his dad cannot find the trail, even with the arrows. What does the box say to do?
options: Stay where they are and call for help
Keep walking in a new direction until they find a trail
Split up so each person can look for the trail
Walk toward the sunset to find the parking lot
items.hint: Find the line that starts with If you cannot find the trail. Read the reason too.
items.explain: They should stay where they are and call for help. The seventh line says this, because staying in one place makes you easier to find.

items.prompt: Ana is cutting carrots. Her knife slides off the counter. What should she do?
options: Grab it with a towel
Step back and let it drop
Catch it by the handle
Put her foot out to stop it
items.hint: Find the sentence about a falling knife. Read both parts of it.
items.explain: Ana should step back and let it drop. The second paragraph says to step back and never try to catch a falling knife.

items.prompt: Priya finishes cutting. The sink is full of soapy water. What should she do with her knife?
options: Push it under the soapy water so it gets very clean
Leave it on the cutting board for the next team
Wash it separately, dry it, and put it back in the knife block
Put it in the sink to soak with the bowls
items.hint: Read the third paragraph. Find what not to do with soapy water, and what to do instead.
items.explain: Priya should wash it separately, dry it and put it back in the knife block. The third paragraph says never to put a knife into a sink full of soapy water, because another person could reach in without seeing it.

items.prompt: Build Ben's plan for carrying a knife across the room.
items.frame: Hold the knife with {0}. Say {1} when you walk past someone.

options: the blade pointing up, in front of you
the blade pointing at the floor, in front of your body
the blade wrapped in a paper towel
the blade pointing down, next to your leg
"Knife behind you"
"Watch out"
"Excuse me"
"Hot pan"

items.hint: Read the third paragraph. Find how to hold the knife and the exact words to say.
items.explain: Hold the knife with the blade pointing down, next to your leg, and say Knife behind you when you walk past someone. Both are at the start of the third paragraph.

items.prompt: Which example password follows all the rules on the screen?
options: violin cactus ladder pancake
PixelRivera2014
trains
SamLovesTrains!
items.hint: Check each password against three rules: how long it is, no names or birthdays, and words that have nothing to do with each other.
items.explain: violin cactus ladder pancake follows all the rules. It has more than 12 characters and joins 4 words that have nothing to do with each other. The others are too short, or they use Sam's name or his dog's name. Make your own password, not this example.

items.prompt: Leo asks for Sam's library password so he can borrow an e-book. What should Sam do?
options: Text the password to Leo, then change it next week
Say no, and help Leo make his own account
Tell Leo, because they are good friends
Tell Leo only the first half
items.hint: Find the line about sharing. Who may know your password?
items.explain: Sam should say no and help Leo make his own account. The last line says never to share your password with friends. Only a parent may know it.

items.prompt: Sam wants to use his new library password for his train game too. What does the screen say?
options: Use the same one, but add his birthday at the end
Use the same one, but for only two accounts
Use a different password for every account
Use the same one, because it is strong
items.hint: Find the rule about more than one account.
items.explain: Use a different password for every account. The fourth line says this.

items.prompt: The weather service says a winter storm watch begins tonight. What does this mean?
options: Heavy snow is falling now, so everyone must stay indoors
The storm has ended, so plows are clearing the streets
A storm will surely hit tomorrow, so the ferry has stopped
A storm is possible in the next two days, so it is time to get ready
items.hint: Find the sentence that explains a watch. Then find the simple way to remember the difference.
items.explain: A storm is possible in the next two days, so it is time to get ready. The first paragraph says a watch means a storm is possible and forecasters are not yet certain, and that a watch means be prepared.

items.prompt: There is a winter storm watch, and no snow has fallen yet. Which job fits this time best?
options: Charge the tablet and put fresh batteries in the flashlights
Stay indoors until the plows clear the streets
Check the school website for a closing by 6:00 AM
Wait for an adult to say the sidewalks are safe
items.hint: The article tells what to do at each stage: during a watch, during a warning, and after the warning ends. Find the paragraph for a watch.
items.explain: Charging the tablet and putting fresh batteries in the flashlights fits a watch. The second paragraph lists these jobs for a watch. The other jobs belong to a warning or to the time after it ends.

items.prompt: Sort each action by when the article says to do it.

cards.text: Check for food and water for three days
Charge phones and tablets
Store extra pet food
Stay indoors
Wait to travel until plows clear the streets
Wait for an adult to say the sidewalks are safe

items.hint: Each stage has its own part of the article. Put each card with the part that names it.
items.explain: Food and water, charging and pet food are in the paragraph about a watch. Staying indoors and waiting for the plows are in the paragraph about a warning. Waiting for an adult to say the sidewalks are safe comes when the warning ends, in the last paragraph.

items.prompt: Suppose Ben taps Get My Pass and changes nothing. How much will he be charged each month after the 3 free days?
items.hint: Find the star after the price, and read the line that starts with the same star. Then check what is already checked for him.
items.explain: $10 each month. The line with the star says the pass costs $8 every month after 3 free days, and Coin Doubler is already checked, which adds $2 a month. $8 plus $2 is $10, which is all of the money his mom gave him.

items.prompt: Ben checks the screen for tricks. Sort each part.

cards.text: $0.00 today, with a small star
Only 3 players can still get this deal
Coin Doubler is already checked for you
A button that says No thanks, I don't like winning
Single items are in the Item Shop
The pass gives new karts and new tracks

items.hint: For each card, ask: does it hide a cost, rush me, choose for me, or try to make me feel bad for saying no? If not, it is plain information.
items.explain: The star hides the monthly cost, the 3 players line rushes Ben, the checked box chooses for him, and the No thanks button tries to make him feel bad for saying no. Where single items are and what the pass gives are plain information.

items.prompt: Ben only wants new wheels for $3. What should he do?
options: Tap the small x to go to the Item Shop, and buy the wheels there
Tap No thanks, I don't like winning, because it is the only way out
Tap Get My Pass, and plan to cancel before the 3 days end
Tap Get My Pass, but uncheck Coin Doubler first
items.hint: Find the line that tells where single items are, and how to get there.
items.explain: Ben should tap the small x and buy the wheels in the Item Shop. The last line says single items are there. The No thanks button is not the only way out, and the pass would cost money every month.

items.prompt: Leo and Sam find a hole in a hillside with old boards over it and no sign. What should they do?
options: Take a quick look inside with a flashlight, then tell a ranger
Stay away from it, mark the spot on their map, and tell a park ranger
Stand on the boards to see if they are strong, then tell a ranger
Throw a rock in to find out how deep it is, then mark the map
items.hint: Read the third paragraph. It tells what to do when an opening has no sign. Check every part of each plan.
items.explain: They should stay away, mark the spot on their map and tell a park ranger. The third paragraph says not to go near an opening with no sign or throw rocks into it, and to tell a ranger. The second paragraph says old boards can break.

items.prompt: Tap the sentence that explains why you cannot tell when the air in a mine is bad.
items.hint: Read the second paragraph. Look for a sentence about air.
items.explain: Tap the sentence that says the air deep inside may not have enough oxygen, and you cannot see or smell the difference. It is in the second paragraph.

items.prompt: What is the main idea of this notice?
options: Miners dug for copper in Lantern Peaks more than a hundred years ago
Bats can fly through the gates over mine openings
Workers check the walls of Ridgeway Mine Museum every day
Old mines in the hills are not safe, so stay out and tell a ranger about openings
items.hint: Ask which choice the whole notice is about. A detail is true, but it comes from only one part.
items.explain: The main idea is that old mines are not safe, so you stay out and tell a ranger about openings. Every paragraph leads to this. The other choices are true details from one part of the notice.

items.prompt: Which request must Priya allow, or RoverLink cannot drive her rover?
options: Bluetooth
Microphone
Location
Contacts
items.hint: Read the note under the table. Then find the row it names for driving.
items.explain: Bluetooth. The note says RoverLink needs Bluetooth to drive the rover, and the Bluetooth row says it is used to connect and drive. The microphone is optional, because the arrow buttons also drive the rover.

items.prompt: Priya's mom says, "Give an app only what it needs, and only for as long as it needs it." Which Camera choice fits her rule best?
options: Allow Always
Allow Once
Allow While Using the App
Don't Allow, and skip the setup
items.hint: Read why RoverLink wants the camera and how many times it needs it. Then choose the shortest choice that still lets the setup work.
items.explain: Allow Once. The Camera row says the app scans the code one time, during setup, and the note says it needs the camera one time. Allow While Using the App would give it more time than it needs, and Allow Always is not a choice for the camera.

items.prompt: Priya and her mom go through the list. Sort each request.

cards.text: Bluetooth, to connect and drive
Camera, to scan the code during setup
Location, to show robot clubs nearby
Contacts, to invite friends
Microphone, for voice commands

items.hint: Read the note under the table first. Then check each row against it.
items.explain: Bluetooth and the camera for setup are needed, because the note says so. Location, contacts and the microphone are optional. The rover can still be driven with the arrow buttons.

items.prompt: The bird walk starts at the Gull Island dock at 12:45 PM. Which is the latest ferry that gets them there in time today?
options: The 12:00 PM ferry
The 11:30 AM ferry
The 2:30 PM ferry
The 9:30 AM ferry
items.hint: Use today's ferry times and the trip time for fog, not the usual ones. Add the trip time to each ferry time.
items.explain: The 9:30 AM ferry. In fog the trip takes 60 minutes, so it arrives at 10:30 AM. The 12:00 PM ferry would arrive at 1:00 PM, which is too late. It would only be in time on a day with the usual 40-minute trip. There is no 11:30 AM ferry today, because every ferry leaves 30 minutes later.

items.prompt: On the ferry, Sam hears the horn again and again. What does the notice say about it?
options: It is normal in fog, and it tells other boats where the ferry is
It means everyone must put on a life jacket
It means the ferry is turning back to Harbor Town
It means passengers may go out on the outer deck
items.hint: Find the line about the horn. Read the reason it gives.
items.explain: It is normal in fog, and it lets other boats know where the ferry is. The fifth line says the horn sounds every 2 minutes for this reason.

items.prompt: They bought tickets for a ferry, but the fog gets thicker and Captain Ruth Lane cancels it. What can they do with their tickets?
options: Use them only after the fog clears today
Use them on any ferry in the next 30 days
Use them only on the next ferry today
Nothing, because the tickets no longer work
items.hint: Find the line about tickets for a canceled ferry.
items.explain: They can use the tickets on any ferry for 30 days. The last line says this, so they can choose another day for the bird walk.

items.prompt: Maya finds a small shark tooth. Then she finds a long, flat piece in the rock that might be bone. What should she do?
options: Dig the bone out slowly with her own tools, then give it to the museum
Give the tooth to the museum, and keep the bone for her rock collection
Keep the tooth, put a yellow flag by the bone, and call a museum worker
Keep both, because she found them herself
items.hint: There are two finds. Find the rule for shells and teeth and the rule for bones. A good plan follows both.
items.explain: Maya should keep the tooth, put a yellow flag by the bone and call a museum worker. The third paragraph says you may keep small shells or shark teeth, that bones belong to the museum, and not to dig out a bone yourself.

items.prompt: Why does the notice say not to dig out a bone yourself?
options: Bones are too heavy to carry to the cars
Only adults are allowed to touch bones
Bones must stay in the quarry for good
Bones break easily when they are pulled from rock
items.hint: Find the sentence about uncovering a bone. Look for the word because.
items.explain: Bones break easily when they are pulled from rock. The third paragraph gives this reason after the word because.

items.prompt: Sort what each person does at the dig.

cards.text: Ben borrows safety glasses at the gate
Ana wears sandals so her feet stay cool
Maya, who is 11, digs next to her dad all morning
Leo steps behind the orange fence to see the cliff
Sam keeps four shells from the dig pile
Priya takes home a fossil bigger than her hand

items.hint: Match each card to one rule in the notice. Check numbers, ages and sizes carefully.
items.explain: Borrowing glasses, digging next to an adult at age 11 and keeping four shells follow the notice. Sandals, going behind the orange fence and taking a fossil bigger than your hand break the rules about boots, the loose cliff and what belongs to the museum.

items.prompt: Leo is 13 and Ana is 12. What must happen before either of them climbs?
options: A staff member checks their harnesses, and they sign the safety forms themselves
An adult signs a safety form for each of them, and a staff member checks their harnesses
Only Ana needs an adult to sign, because Leo is a teenager
Neither needs a form, because both are older than 8
items.hint: Check the age rule against both ages. Then check what happens before every first climb.
items.explain: An adult signs a safety form for each of them, and a staff member checks their harnesses. The first rule says climbers under 14 need an adult to sign, and both are under 14. The second rule says staff check every harness before the first climb.

items.prompt: Put Ana's steps for her first climb in order.
steps: Put on a harness and have a staff member check it.
Clip the auto-belay to the front loop and check that the gate is closed.
Climb a green route to the top.
Let go of the wall and lean back while the auto-belay lowers her.
items.hint: Think about what must happen before she leaves the ground, then what happens on the wall, then at the top.
items.explain: First Ana puts on a harness and has it checked. Then she clips the auto-belay to the front loop and checks the gate. Next she climbs a green route, because the board says to start on green. At the top she lets go and leans back.

items.prompt: Ana is halfway up a rope. Leo wants to clip onto the same rope and climb below her so they can race. What does the board say?
options: Climb, but stay far below Ana
Climb, if both of them check their gates first
Climb on the same rope, but take a blue route
Wait until Ana is back on the ground, because only one climber may be on each rope
items.hint: Find the rule about how many climbers can be on a rope. Read both parts of it.
items.explain: Leo should wait until Ana is back on the ground. The fifth rule says only one climber on each rope at a time, and never to climb above or below another person.

items.prompt: It is bedtime at the campsite. Sam has toothpaste and a granola bar in his backpack in the tent. What should he do?
options: Put both in the food locker and close the latch
Put the granola bar in the locker, but keep the toothpaste in the tent
Keep both in the backpack, but zip it tightly
Eat the granola bar, and keep the toothpaste in his sleeping bag
items.hint: Check the rule for food and the rule for things with a strong smell. Then check the rule about tents.
items.explain: Sam should put both in the food locker and close the latch. The second paragraph says to store food and things with a strong smell, such as toothpaste, in the locker, and never to keep them in your tent. Raccoons can open zippers.

items.prompt: A fox walks into the campsite while Pixel is on his leash. What should Sam do?
options: Walk slowly toward the fox so he can touch it gently
Stand up, speak in a loud voice, give the fox space to leave, and keep Pixel on the leash
Toss the fox a piece of bread so it will go away
Let Pixel off the leash to chase the fox away
items.hint: Read the third paragraph. Check each plan against every rule in it.
items.explain: Sam should stand up, speak loudly, give the fox space and keep Pixel on the leash. The third paragraph says never to feed wild animals, not to chase or touch them, and to keep pets on a leash.

items.prompt: Which title fits this notice best?
options: How to Choose a Campsite in Story Woods
What to Do When a Fox Visits
Keep Food and Smells Away From Wild Animals
Raccoons Can Open Coolers and Zippers
items.hint: A good title fits every paragraph, not just one or two sentences.
items.explain: Keep Food and Smells Away From Wild Animals fits best. The first paragraph says why people food is bad for animals, the second tells how to store food and smells, and the third says never to feed animals. Raccoons and foxes are details from one part.

items.prompt: The student next to Leo has a blue star sticker on her music folder. What should Leo's dad do?
options: Film the whole row, because he is filming his own child
Film that student only during the bows
Film everyone, but post the video only on the family page
Film Leo, but keep that student out of the video
items.hint: Read the line about blue stars. Then read the line about whom you may film.
items.explain: He should film Leo but keep that student out of the video. The program says you may film your own child, and families of students with a blue star asked that they not appear in any photos or videos.

items.prompt: Sort what people do at the concert.

cards.text: A flash photo during the bows
A flash photo during the second song
A close video of Leo's drum part
A close video of a student with a blue star
Posting Leo's video on the family page
Posting Leo's video on a public site
Holding a bright phone up high during a song

items.hint: Match each card to a rule. Watch for words about time, like during the music and during the bows.
items.explain: A flash photo during the bows, a close video of your own child and posting on the family page follow the rules. Flash or a bright phone during a song, filming a blue-star student and posting on a public site break them.

items.prompt: Leo's grandma could not come, and she is not a school family. How can she see the whole concert without anyone breaking a rule?
options: She can log in to the family page with Leo's dad's password
Leo's family can show her Ms. Gray's full recording when it comes next week
Leo's dad can post his video on a public site for her
Leo's dad can film the whole band up close for her
items.hint: Find who can see the family page and what Ms. Gray will share. Then find the plan that breaks no rule.
items.explain: Leo's family can show her Ms. Gray's full recording next week. The last line says every family gets it. Posting on a public site and filming other students up close are against the rules, and a password should never be shared.

items.prompt: Sam's oven mitt got wet when he washed a bowl. Grandma Rose says the cookies are ready. What should Sam do?
options: Use a damp towel instead of the mitt
Use the wet mitt, because it is only a little wet
Get a dry mitt, and ask Grandma Rose if he may open the oven
Use the wet mitt quickly, before the cookies burn
items.hint: Check the rule about mitts and the rule about the oven. A safe plan follows both.
items.explain: Sam should get a dry mitt and ask Grandma Rose if he may open the oven. The third rule says to use only dry mitts, because a wet mitt lets heat through. The last rule says to ask Grandma Rose before you use the oven.

items.prompt: Maya just spread peanut butter on her lunch at the front table. Now she wants to help at the back table. What should she do?
options: Wipe the knife on a towel, then use it at the back table
Bring the knife, but use it only to spread jam
Wash the knife, but not her hands, because her hands look clean
Wash her hands, and leave the peanut butter knife at the front table
items.hint: Read the rule about the back table. It has two parts: one about hands and one about what may come to the table.
items.explain: Maya should wash her hands and leave the peanut butter knife at the front table. The rule says to wash your hands before you work at the back table and never to bring nut butters or tools from other tables to it.

items.prompt: Sort what Sam and Maya do in the kitchen.

cards.text: Sam scrapes the bowl after the beater stops moving
Maya touches the beater while it is still slowing down
Sam puts out the Wet Floor sign, then gets the mop
Maya tastes a spoonful of raw cookie dough
Sam washes his hands after he cracks eggs
Maya gets the mop first and puts out the sign after

items.hint: Match each card to one rule. Check the order words carefully: before, after, first.
items.explain: Scraping after the beater stops, putting out the sign before the mop, and washing after eggs follow the rules. Touching a beater that is still moving, tasting raw dough and getting the mop before the sign break them.

steps.say: Maya wants to keep her comic. So I need the button that keeps it.
I read the box. It asks if she wants to delete Comic Page 3.
The next line says you cannot get it back. Delete means it is gone for good.
Cancel means stop. Nothing gets deleted.
So Maya taps Cancel. When I am not sure, I keep the file.
